principles: Un-gameable RED: a RED record must prove a real failing run against the real target at a specific tree state, and GREEN must prove the same assertion now passes.
Spec-before-code: define contracts precisely enough (field schemas, digests, state transitions, gate-consumption rules) that implementation stories are mechanical, deferring all code.
Append-only auditable history: supersession is explicit and integrity-checked; nothing is silently replaced or deleted.
Owner-gated non-destructive corrections: quarantine and recover create NEW linked records and never mutate prior records.
Draw the W2/W3 boundary explicitly: the subsystem exposes a stable query that gates consume; enforcement wiring stays out of scope.
drivers: The subsystem sits on gate-trust code where a silent design error becomes a forged-evidence hole.
The program plan sequences a PLAN-reviewed spec story before implementation; this story ships only the decision document.
In-flight stories already hold red-evidence.json records, so the design must not disrupt them mid-program.

options.name: spec-first decision document
pros: Matches program sequencing (spec story, then implementation stories).
Cross-host PLAN review catches design holes before any gate-trust code is written.
Implementation stories cite sections as acceptance contracts, keeping them mechanical.
Zero runtime risk in this story.
cons: Adds a story before working value ships.
Spec precision must be high or implementation stories re-open the design.

options.name: implement-directly
cons: Design errors in gate-trust code become forged-evidence holes with no PLAN review.
Violates the program sequencing that R2-R4 audits demanded.
No citable contract for later section-level verification.

options.name: extend-existing-schema-ad-hoc
cons: No coherent envelope/chain/idempotency design, so partial guarantees stay gameable.
The append-only store keeps its silent-replace hole.
Accumulates un-audited drift the program explicitly rejected across R2-R4.

rationale: The program plan mandates a PLAN-reviewed spec before implementation precisely because this subsystem is gate-trust code; authoring the contracts as a reviewed, cross-host-audited document lets review find design holes before any forged-evidence risk is introduced, and gives the W2 implementation stories citable section-level acceptance contracts.

preMortem.scenario: Spec over-constrains the runner so it is unimplementable in the macOS sandbox.
preMortem.trigger: Four-tuple invariance is specified to require an isolation mechanism (container/overlay/root) unavailable to a sandboxed runner.
preMortem.consequence: W2 implementation stories cannot satisfy the spec and re-open the design, stalling the program.
preMortem.mitigation: Spec the disposable workspace as a plain filesystem-level temp copy/worktree with a portable pre/post snapshot, explicitly avoiding container/root requirements, and record macOS-sandbox compatibility as an acceptance constraint.

preMortem.scenario: Envelope minimum-specificity rule is too strict and rejects every legitimate RED.
preMortem.trigger: The bounded-matcher threshold is set so aggressively that normal failing-assertion patterns fall below it.
preMortem.consequence: Real RED evidence is rejected, blocking honest stories and pressuring users to game the gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Define minimum-specificity as a policy-owned tunable lower bound with a worked accept/reject example set in the spec, using the vacuous zero-line pattern as the canonical reject rather than a hard-coded constant.

preMortem.scenario: Supersedes-chain integrity check is too weak and a fork goes undetected.
preMortem.trigger: Chain validation checks seq monotonicity but not the prior-record digest link, so a parallel record can splice in.
preMortem.consequence: Two chain heads exist and a fabricated record masquerades as the latest RED, defeating the gate.
preMortem.mitigation: Spec requires ALL of monotonic seq + prior-record digest match + explicit fork rejection yielding a single unique chain head, with an adversarial fork example that MUST be rejected as an acceptance check.

preMortem.scenario: Legacy posture invalidates the records of in-flight stories mid-program.
preMortem.trigger: The spec declares existing red-evidence.json records invalid on adoption with no migration or grandfather path.
preMortem.consequence: Stories mid-flight lose their RED evidence and are blocked at their next gate, causing a program-wide stall.
preMortem.mitigation: Spec must state an explicit legacy posture (grandfather or migrate) with a compatibility rule that keeps pre-subsystem records gate-satisfying until superseded, and forbids silent invalidation without a stated rule.
